# xmppd Configuration

<!-- Generated by `zig build docs-config` from src/config/schema.zig. Do not edit. -->

All configuration lives in a single INI file shared by every daemon, selected
with `--config PATH` (`-c`). `xmppd-auth-oidc` defaults to
`/usr/local/etc/xmppd/xmppd.conf` when `--config` is absent. Precedence is
default < file < CLI, tracked per field, with the master's resolved values
forwarded to its children in between (see "Config forwarding" below). An
unknown section or key, a bad value, or a malformed line is a startup error
that names the file and line; defaults live only in the schema
(`src/config/schema.zig`), so `xmppd --help` is the authoritative option
list.

## File keys

Every key the shared file may carry, grouped by section. Fields that
take no file key (`in_file = false` in the schema) are CLI-only and
listed under the daemon that accepts them.

### [server]

| Key | Default | Used by | Description |
|-----|---------|---------|-------------|
| `hostname` | `localhost` | core, s2s | XMPP domain served (e.g., `example.com`); set it for any real deployment |
| `bind_address` | `0.0.0.0` | master, core, s2s | C2S listen address literal; S2S follows it unless `s2s.bind_address` is set |
| `c2s_port` | `5222` | master, core | Client-to-server port |
| `db_path` | `/var/db/xmppd` | master, core, auth, oidc, ctl | Storage base directory; the master also creates `auth/`, `op/`, `archive/` subdirectories under it |
| `lmdb_map_size_mb` | `8192` | auth, oidc | LMDB map size in MiB; fixed at open, never resized at runtime |
| `user` | (none) | master | Unprivileged user the master's children run as (required when the master runs as root) |
| `log_file` | `/var/log/xmppd/xmppd.log` | master | Log file path (used with `--background`) |
| `pidfile` | `/var/run/xmppd/xmppd.pid` | (none yet) | PID file path; no daemon reads it yet (the master writes `{run_dir}/xmppd.pid`) |

### [tls]

| Key | Default | Used by | Description |
|-----|---------|---------|-------------|
| `cert` | (none) | core, s2s | TLS certificate path (PEM, full chain) |
| `key` | (none) | core, s2s | TLS private key path (PEM) |
| `enabled` | `true` | core, s2s | Enable TLS (C2S STARTTLS and s2s) |

### [auth]

| Key | Default | Used by | Description |
|-----|---------|---------|-------------|
| `socket` | `/var/run/xmppd/auth.sock` | master, core, auth, oidc, ctl | Auth daemon IPC socket; also the default for `oidc.socket` |
| `max_per_account` | `60` | auth, oidc | Max auth attempts per account per window (alias `rate_max_per_account`) |
| `max_per_ip` | `200` | auth, oidc | Max auth attempts per IP per window (alias `rate_max_per_ip`) |
| `window_seconds` | `120` | auth, oidc | Rate window size in seconds |
| `lockout_duration` | `5m` | auth, oidc | Temporary lockout (`300`, `300s` and `5m` are equivalent) |
| `lockout_threshold` | `10` | auth, oidc | Consecutive account failures before temporary lockout |
| `ip_lockout_threshold` | `20` | auth, oidc | Consecutive IP failures before that address is temporarily locked |
| `users_scan_limit` | `100000` | auth | Startup users scan bound |
| `rate_limit` | `true` | auth, oidc | Rate limiting master switch; `false` disables it entirely (testing/benchmarks only) |
| `crypto_threads` | `4` | auth | Password hash threads (`0` disables the pool and derives inline) |
| `registration` | `false` | auth | In-band registration (XEP-0077) |
| `require_invite` | `true` | auth | Require invitation code for registration |
| `login_rate_ceiling` | `512` | auth | Sustained SCRAM login rate the replay cache is sized for (capacity = ceiling x nonce window) |
| `scram_nonce_window_seconds` | `60` | auth | Seconds a core-minted server nonce stays consumable; also the replay-cache entry TTL |
| `scram_nonce_skew_seconds` | `15` | auth | Seconds of forward clock skew tolerated on server-nonce timestamps |

### [s2s]

| Key | Default | Used by | Description |
|-----|---------|---------|-------------|
| `socket` | `/var/run/xmppd/s2s.sock` | master, core, s2s | IPC socket between core and xmppd-s2s |
| `port` | `5269` | master, s2s | S2S listening port |
| `enabled` | `true` | master, core | Enable s2s federation; the master skips the child and core does not connect |
| `bind_address` | (follows `server.bind_address`) | master, s2s | S2S listen address literal |

`listen_fd` is CLI-only: a file key naming it is an unknown-key error.

### [muc]

| Key | Default | Used by | Description |
|-----|---------|---------|-------------|
| `host` | `conference.{hostname}` | core, s2s | MUC service domain; empty resolves to `conference.{server.hostname}` |

### [core]

| Key | Default | Used by | Description |
|-----|---------|---------|-------------|
| `max_sessions` | `4096` | core | Maximum concurrent C2S sessions, divided evenly across workers |
| `fan_out_batch_size` | `32` | core | MUC occupants delivered per loop tick before yielding |
| `max_resources_per_account` | `256` | core | Maximum resources per account |
| `scram_exchange_slots` | `256` | core | Concurrent in-flight SCRAM logins per worker; a full pool answers temporary-auth-failure |
| `workers` | `auto` | master | C2S listener count; `auto` detects CPUs |
| `log_level` | `info` | (none yet) | Log verbosity (`debug`, `info`, `warn`, `err`); no daemon reads it yet (`std_options` pins `info`) |

`listen_fd` is CLI-only: a file key naming it is an unknown-key error.

### [oidc]

Required when `[master] auth_path` points at xmppd-auth-oidc; ignored otherwise.

| Key | Default | Used by | Description |
|-----|---------|---------|-------------|
| `issuer` | (required) | oidc | OIDC issuer URL; must match the token `iss` claim |
| `client_id` | (required) | oidc | OAuth2 client ID |
| `client_secret` | (required) | oidc | OAuth2 client secret |
| `token_endpoint` | (required) | oidc | Token endpoint URL (for ROPC) |
| `jwks_uri` | (required) | oidc | JWKS endpoint URL (for JWT key fetching) |
| `ca_file` | (none) | oidc | CA bundle path for IdP TLS verification |
| `introspection_endpoint` | (none) | oidc | RFC 7662 introspection (for opaque tokens) |
| `user_domain` | (none) | oidc | Domain appended to bare usernames for ROPC (e.g., `morante.dev`) |
| `socket` | (follows `[auth] socket`) | oidc | OIDC-specific IPC socket override |
| `max_per_account` | `60` | oidc | Max requests per account; `[auth] max_per_account` wins at equal provenance (alias `rate_max_per_account`) |
| `max_per_ip` | `200` | oidc | Max requests per IP; `[auth] max_per_ip` wins at equal provenance (alias `rate_max_per_ip`) |
| `rate_limit` | `true` | oidc | Rate limiting switch |
| `import_avatar` | `false` | oidc, core | Import the IdP `picture` claim into the vCard on first login |
| `idp_threads` | `8` | oidc | IdP HTTP client threads (1..32) |
| `idp_max_outstanding` | `256` | oidc | Max in-flight IdP requests (1..4096) |
| `idp_connect_timeout_ms` | `3000` | oidc | IdP connect timeout in ms (100..60000) |
| `idp_timeout_ms` | `10000` | oidc | IdP request timeout in ms (connect timeout..120000) |
| `localpart_claim` | `preferred_username` | oidc | Claim supplying the first-login localpart suggestion: `preferred_username`, `email`, `sub`, or empty to disable auto-provisioning |
| `localpart_claim_prefix` | (none) | oidc | Prefix stripped from the suggestion claim before PRECIS preparation (e.g., `user:` for handle-form subjects) |
| `localpart_auto_suffix` | `false` | oidc | When the suggested localpart is taken, try `lp-2` .. `lp-99`; `false` refuses a taken suggestion instead |

#### Account binding

XMPP accounts bind permanently to the `(iss, sub)` pair (OIDC Core 5.7):
once a subject logs in, its mapping in `{db}/auth` (`oidc_identities`
namespace) decides the account forever, and renamed IdP claims cannot
re-map it. The `localpart_claim` value is only a first-login
*suggestion*: it never binds identity. The suggestion is prepared with
the same RFC 7622 UsernameCaseMapped localpart function as registration
(`NaplesTB` suggests `naplestb`), so two different claims that prepare to
one localpart collide and the second is refused. A suggestion is refused
when the localpart is already bound to another subject, when a provisioned
`users` row exists, or when the account already owns roster, archive or
MUC data (upgrade installs must run `xmppctl oidc-unclaimed` and
`oidc-link` first; see UPGRADING.md). `localpart_claim = email` is
accepted only when the IdP reports `email_verified = true` and is the
weakest choice because email is editable at most IdPs. Setting
`localpart_claim` to an empty string disables auto-provisioning
entirely: every account then needs an explicit `xmppctl oidc-link`.
Local registration runs the reverse index too: XEP-0077 registration and
`xmppctl add` refuse a localpart bound to a subject (`conflict`, and a
bound-localpart error at the ctl) instead of attaching a password
credential to the bound account.

Claiming a localpart is a conditional write that must hold against every
process that can open `{db}/auth` (`xmppd-auth-oidc`, the core daemon,
`xmppctl`, and any second auth daemon). Only the LMDB and SQLite
backends serialize that check across processes; RocksDB orders
`putIfAbsent` with an in-process mutex, so `xmppd-auth-oidc` refuses to
start when the operational storage backend is RocksDB. OIDC account
binding requires `-Dop-storage=lmdb` (the default) or
`-Dop-storage=sqlite`.

| IdP | Recommended keys | Notes |
|-----|------------------|-------|
| identity-oidc | `localpart_claim = sub`, `localpart_claim_prefix = user:` | While subject IDs are handle-form (`user:name`), strip the prefix. After identityd issue #52 lands opaque subjects, use an admin-controlled preferred username instead. |
| Rauthy | `localpart_claim = preferred_username` | Safe only with immutable usernames and controlled provisioning. `email` is unsafe: it is user-editable and `email_fallback` makes it self-selected. |
| Keycloak | `localpart_claim = preferred_username` | Safe only when username edits are forbidden and provisioning is controlled. Otherwise use `localpart_claim =` (empty) plus operator links. |

### [master]

| Key | Default | Used by | Description |
|-----|---------|---------|-------------|
| `core_path` | `xmppd-core` | master | Core binary path |
| `auth_path` | `xmppd-auth` | master | Auth binary path (or `xmppd-auth-oidc`) |
| `s2s_path` | `xmppd-s2s` | master | S2S federation binary path |

`run_dir` and `background` are CLI-only: a file key naming one is an unknown-key error.

## Example

```ini
[server]
hostname = example.com
user = jabber
db_path = /var/db/xmppd
log_file = /var/log/xmppd/xmppd.log

[tls]
cert = /usr/local/etc/xmppd/fullchain.pem
key = /usr/local/etc/xmppd/privkey.pem

[core]
max_sessions = 4096

[muc]
host = conference.example.com

[master]
core_path = /usr/local/libexec/xmppd/xmppd-core
auth_path = /usr/local/libexec/xmppd/xmppd-auth
```

## OIDC Example

```ini
[master]
auth_path = /usr/local/libexec/xmppd/xmppd-auth-oidc

[oidc]
issuer = https://auth.example.com/auth/v1/
client_id = xmppd
client_secret = your-client-secret
token_endpoint = https://auth.example.com/auth/v1/oidc/token
jwks_uri = https://auth.example.com/auth/v1/oidc/certs
user_domain = example.com
ca_file = /usr/local/etc/xmppd/ca-bundle.pem
```

## CLI Flags

All binaries accept `--config PATH` (`-c`) to specify the config file
location. Each `--help` below is produced by the shared loader from
the same schema, so it cannot drift from what the parser accepts.
Only the master prints the file-key table after its options; the
list is the shared grammar above and is identical for every daemon.

### xmppd-auth-oidc

```
Options:
  --config, -c <CONFIG>  config file path
  --db <DB>  storage base directory
  --socket <SOCKET>  auth IPC socket path
```

Without `--config` or `--conf-fd`, xmppd-auth-oidc reads
`/usr/local/etc/xmppd/xmppd.conf`.

### xmppctl

```
Options:
  --db <DB>  storage directory
  --auth-socket <AUTH-SOCKET>  auth daemon IPC socket
  --password <PASSWORD>  provide password non-interactively
  --password-file <PASSWORD-FILE>  read password from file
  --apply  apply migration ops (default dry run)
  --raw  deluser: exact source localpart
  --run-dir <RUN-DIR>  daemon pid-file directory
  --max-uses <MAX-USES>  invite create: max uses
  --expires <EXPIRES>  invite create: hours until expiry
  --config, -c <CONFIG>  config file path
  --help, -h  show this help
```

`xmppctl` also takes subcommand positionals it pre-scans itself:
`--hosted-domain` (repeatable, a list the schema cannot express) and
`--rename OLD NEW` (two values). A subcommand that is not a known
verb is a usage error.

Unknown arguments, unknown file keys, malformed lines, non-numeric values,
and values outside the consuming daemon's bounds are startup errors with a
`file:line` diagnostic when they came from a file. Rate maxima above 65535,
a zero rate window, and a lockout that is not a whole number of seconds are
errors rather than values to clamp or replace with defaults.

## Config forwarding

The master forwards the *resolved* values to every child. After loading
the file and its own CLI it serializes the effective fields once into a
sealed in-memory fd that `xmppd-auth` (either backend), `xmppd-core`, and
`xmppd-s2s` inherit through the supervisor's `pass_fds` remap, named on
their argv as `--conf-fd N`. Their precedence is therefore
default < file < forwarded < CLI: a file key or a master CLI flag
(`xmppd -c xmppd.conf --host x.test`) reaches every child exactly once,
and a child-side CLI flag still wins for a manual run. Child argv carries
only fd remap slots (`--listen-fd` where applicable and `--conf-fd`). A
child started by hand without `--conf-fd` reads `--config` directly. On
SIGHUP the master rebuilds the fd from the reloaded configuration before
forwarding the signal, so a respawned child sees the new values; no
supervised child re-reads the file.
